category_title: Students proactively seeking support to avoid triggers
minimal_context: Landry is meeting with the teacher between classes to prepare for writing a poem in response to trauma literature.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Thanks for stopping by between classes. Today we will be writing a poem as a creative response to the novel Speak and the complementary texts.

STUDENT: I began a poem. It starts with, 'The screams in the air are thick / I can feel her pain in my lungs.'

TUTOR: Okay, keep working on that during the lesson.

STUDENT: I am trying to take steps for my comfort and safety to avoid triggering.

TUTOR: Just follow along with the reading when class starts.

STUDENT: That's why I asked for this check-in. I need to discuss the specific details of today's lesson right now so I am not caught off guard.

options.A: Ask an explain-story-element question to prompt the student to analyze the novel and complementary trauma texts.
options.B: Conduct a private check-in to discuss the specific details of the day's lesson before class begins.
options.C: Use the poem as an entry point to focus mainly on language to support purpose and meaning.
options.D: Ask a follow-up question that links the physical sensation in the poem to a potential emotional state.
